review.stem:
A 41 year old male veterinarian consults you because of
a tender mass in his left axillary region. Upon PE, there
was axillary lymphadenopathy on his right axilla. Upon
further examination you noted several scratch marks
on his right forearm. The causative organism of the
above case is also associated with which disease in
immunocompromised individuals?
review.explanation:
Bartonella henselae
A. Cat-Scratch Disease
Cat-scratch disease is usually a benign, self-
limited illness, manifested by fever and
lymphadenopathy that develop 1–3 weeks
after contact with a cat (usually a scratch,
lick, bite, or perhaps a flea bite). A primary
skin lesion (papule or pustule) develops at
the site J Jawetz Medical Microbiology 27th
ed p. 305 (Bartonella is also the causative
agent of Bacillary angiomatosis)

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: 25-year old male is admitted to the hospital with testicular pain. Physical examination reveals a swollen and inflamed right testis. CT scan examination reveals abnormal accumulation of fluid in the cavity of the tunica vaginalis. Which of the following conditions will MOST accurately describe the signs observed in the patient?
review.explanation: In the true hydrocele, there is a collection of fluid in some part of the processus vaginalis. The types may be vaginal, congenital, infantile and hydroceles of the cord. The vaginal type presents a collection of fluid, not due to any fault of development, in the tunica vaginalis. The congenital (intermittent) type is due to a tiny communication between processus vaginalis and peritoneal cavity. In infantile type, the processus vaginalis is occluded only at the internal abdominal ring. In hydrocele of the cord, the funicular process fails to shrink to a fibrous cord so that a tubular cavity results.

choiceRationales.A: Varicocele is characterized by the dilation of the veins within the scrotum, often described as a "bag of worms." It typically presents as a painless swelling and is more common on the left side due to the anatomy of the venous drainage. Physical examination might reveal a palpable mass, but it is not associated with the accumulation of fluid in the tunica vaginalis.
choiceRationales.B: In the true hydrocele, there is a collection of fluid in some part of the processus vaginalis. The types may be vaginal, congenital, infantile and hydroceles of the cord. The vaginal type presents a collection of fluid, not due to any fault of development, in the tunica vaginalis. The congenital (intermittent) type is due to a tiny communication between processus vaginalis and peritoneal cavity. In infantile type, the processus vaginalis is occluded only at the internal abdominal ring. In hydrocele of the cord, the funicular process fails to shrink to a fibrous cord so that a tubular cavity results.
choiceRationales.C:
Cystocele is a condition where the bladder herniates into the vagina. It is not related to scrotal pain, testicular inflammation, or fluid accumulation in the tunica vaginalis. This choice is not applicable to the patient's presentation.
Grade 1—mildest form, where the bladder drops only partway into the vagina
Grade 2—moderate form, where the bladder has sunken far enough to reach the opening of the vagina
Grade 3—most severe form, where the bladder sags through the opening of the vagina
choiceRationales.D: Rectocele involves the rectum bulging into the back wall of the vagina. Similar to cystocele, it is unrelated to scrotal symptoms and is not a cause of testicular pain or inflammation.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 42-year old mother of three children visits the outpatient clinic complaining that her youngest son cannot walk yet. Radiographic and physical examinations reveals an unstable hip joint. Which of the following ligaments is responsible for stabilization of the hip joint in childhood?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ligament of the head of the femur

review.explanation: The iliofemoral ligament, also known as the "inverted Y ligament of Bigelow," is the most important ligament reinforcing the joint anteriorly. It plays a crucial role in resisting both hyperextension and lateral rotation at the hip joint. This ligament is particularly significant in providing stability to the hip joint in childhood.

choiceRationales.A: The ischiofemoral ligament reinforces the joint posteriorly and limits extension and medial rotation. It is involved in preventing excessive movement in these directions, contributing to the overall stability of the hip joint.
choiceRationales.B:
The ligament of the head of the femur (round ligament of the femur, foveal ligament, or Fillmore’s ligament) is a weak ligament located in the hip joint. It is triangular in shape and somewhat flattened. The ligament is implanted by its apex into the anterosuperior part of the fovea capitis femoris and its base is attached by two bands, one into either side of the acetabular notch, and between these bony attachments it blends with the transverse ligament.
Located deep in the hip, it has a pyramidal shape with a broad origin from nearly the entire transverse acetabular ligament attaching to the ischial and pubic bases by two bundles, with the posterior bundle being stronger than the anterior bundle. The ligamentum teres’ function prior to puberty has been well-described as it provides a secondary blood supply to the head of the femur. However, its function in adulthood is a subject of debate. In a recent meta-analysis of several cadaveric studies, O’Donnell, et al. concluded that the ligamentum teres acts as a secondary stabilizer to supplement the work of the capsular ligaments.
choiceRationales.C: The pubofemoral ligament reinforces the joint inferiorly and prevents hyperabduction. It plays a role in limiting excessive abduction, contributing to the overall stability of the hip joint.
choiceRationales.D: The iliofemoral ligament, also known as the "inverted Y ligament of Bigelow," is the most important ligament reinforcing the joint anteriorly. It plays a crucial role in resisting both hyperextension and lateral rotation at the hip joint. This ligament is particularly significant in providing stability to the hip joint in childhood.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 56-year-old patient has an artificial cardiac pacemaker. Which of the following conductive tissues of the heart had a defective function that required the pacemaker?
review.explanation: The SA node initiates the impulse of contraction and is known as the pacemaker of the heart. Impulses from the SA node travel through the atrial myocardium to the AV node and then race through the AV bundle (bundle of His), which divides into the right and left bundle branches. The bundle breaks up into terminal conducting fibers (Purkinje fibers) to spread out into the ventricular walls. The moderate band carries the right limb of the AV bundle from the septum to the sternocostal wall of the ventricle.

choiceRationales.A: The AV bundle, also known as the bundle of His, is a part of the heart's electrical conduction system. It transmits the electrical impulses from the atria to the ventricles. If there is a defect in the function of the AV bundle, it can lead to heart block, disrupting the normal transmission of signals between the atria and ventricles. However, pacemakers are not typically required for AV bundle issues unless the block is severe.
choiceRationales.B: Purkinje fibers are specialized fibers that conduct electrical impulses, stimulating the contraction of the ventricles. If there is a defect in the Purkinje fibers' function, it can lead to disturbances in ventricular conduction. Pacemakers are not commonly used to address issues specifically related to Purkinje fiber dysfunction.
choiceRationales.C: The atrioventricular (AV) node is another part of the heart's conduction system that slows down the electrical signal before it reaches the ventricles. If there is a defect in the AV node's function, it can lead to heart block and other conduction abnormalities. However, pacemakers are not typically required for AV node dysfunction unless the block is severe.
choiceRationales.D: The SA node initiates the impulse of contraction and is known as the pacemaker of the heart. Impulses from the SA node travel through the atrial myocardium to the AV node and then race through the AV bundle (bundle of His), which divides into the right and left bundle branches. The bundle breaks up into terminal conducting fibers (Purkinje fibers) to spread out into the ventricular walls. The moderate band carries the right limb of the AV bundle from the septum to the sternocostal wall of the ventricle.

review.stem: A patient with a deep stab wound in the middle of the forearm as impaired movement of the thumb. Examination indicates a lesion of the anterior interosseous nerve. Which of the following muscles is paralyzed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flexor pollicis brevis and pronator quadratus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flexor digitorum profundus and pronator quadratus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flexor pollicis longus and opponens pollicis

review.explanation:
The anterior interosseous nerve is a branch of the median nerve at the radiohumeral joint line and supplies the flexor pollicis longus, half of the flexor digitorum profundus, and the pronator quadratus. It has sensory fibers to volar wrist joint capsule with no cutaneous innervation.
The median nerve supplies the pronator teres, flexor digitorum superficialis, palmaris longus, and flexor carpi radialis muscles. A muscular branch (the recurrent branch) of the median nerve innervates the thenar muscles.

choiceRationales.A: The anterior interosseous nerve (AIN) primarily innervates the deep muscles of the forearm. Flexor pollicis brevis is not innervated by the AIN; it is innervated by the median nerve. However, pronator quadratus is innervated by the AIN. So, this choice is partially correct.
choiceRationales.B:
The anterior interosseous nerve is a branch of the median nerve at the radiohumeral joint line and supplies the flexor pollicis longus, half of the flexor digitorum profundus, and the pronator quadratus. It has sensory fibers to volar wrist joint capsule with no cutaneous innervation.
The median nerve supplies the pronator teres, flexor digitorum superficialis, palmaris longus, and flexor carpi radialis muscles. A muscular branch (the recurrent branch) of the median nerve innervates the thenar muscles.
choiceRationales.C: The flexor pollicis longus is primarily innervated by the anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve, not the AIN. Opponens pollicis is innervated by the median nerve as well. This choice is not consistent with the AIN lesion.
choiceRationales.D: Both flexor digitorum profundus and superficialis are primarily innervated by the median nerve, not the AIN. Therefore, this choice is not accurate in the context of an AIN lesion.

review.stem: A first-year resident in the urology department reviews pelvic anatomy before seeing patients. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The duct of the bulbourethral gland opens into the membranous urethra.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The duct of the greater vestibular gland opens into the vagina.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dorsal artery of the penis supplies the glans penis.

review.explanation: The dorsal artery of the penis supplies the glans penis. This artery is a branch of the internal pudendal artery and provides blood to various structures in the penis, including the glans.

choiceRationales.A: The duct of the bulbourethral gland, or Cowper's gland, opens into the bulbous portion of the spongy urethra. These glands secrete a clear, viscous fluid that helps lubricate and neutralize acidic conditions in the urethra before the passage of sperm during ejaculation.
choiceRationales.B: The duct of the greater vestibular gland, also known as Bartholin's gland, opens into the vestibule between the labium minora and the hymen. The gland secretes mucus to lubricate the vulva and vagina.
choiceRationales.C:
This statement is incorrect. The seminal vesicles produce seminal fluid, which is rich in fructose and other substances that nourish and facilitate the motility of sperm. However, they do not store sperm. Sperm are stored in the epididymis.
The Seminal Vesicles produce 90% of the semen which gives off fluorescence under UV light
choiceRationales.D: The dorsal artery of the penis supplies the glans penis. This artery is a branch of the internal pudendal artery and provides blood to various structures in the penis, including the glans.

review.stem: A thoracentesis is performed to aspirate an abnormal accumulation of fluid in a 4-year old patient with pleural effusion. A needle should be inserted at the midaxilliary line between which of the following two ribs as to avoid puncturing the lung?
review.explanation: A thoracentesis is performed for aspiration of fluid in the pleural cavity at or posterior to the midaxillary line one or two intercostal spaces below the fluid level but not below the ninth intercostal space and, therefore, between ribs 7 and 9. Other intercostals spaces are not preferred.

choiceRationales.A: The insertion of the needle between ribs 3 and 5 would place it in a position that's generally higher on the chest wall. This is not the typical location for a thoracentesis, and it might risk injury to structures such as the lungs. It's generally recommended to perform a thoracentesis in the lower intercostal spaces.
choiceRationales.B: The insertion of the needle between ribs 1 and 3 would also be higher on the chest wall and is not a typical site for thoracentesis. This positioning may risk injury to structures like the lungs or other nearby structures.
choiceRationales.C: A thoracentesis is performed for aspiration of fluid in the pleural cavity at or posterior to the midaxillary line one or two intercostal spaces below the fluid level but not below the ninth intercostal space and, therefore, between ribs 7 and 9. Other intercostals spaces are not preferred.
choiceRationales.D: Placing the needle between ribs 5 and 7 would be lower on the chest wall, which could be below the recommended level for thoracentesis. This positioning might increase the risk of injuring structures like the diaphragm.

review.stem: A 47 year old patient complains of chest pain and headache. CT scan reveals a tumor located just superior to the root of the right lung. Blood flow in which of the following veins is most likely blocked by this tumor?
review.explanation:
The correct answer. The arch of the azygos vein, or azygos arch, is a venous channel that arches over the root of the right lung, connecting the superior vena cava to the azygos vein. It receives blood from the posterior intercostal veins and serves as an important collateral pathway. A tumor located just superior to the root of the right lung could potentially block the blood flow in the arch of the azygos vein, leading to symptoms like chest pain and headache.
The azygos vein arches over the root of the right lung and empties into the SVC. Other veins do not pass over the root of the right lung.

choiceRationales.A: The right brachiocephalic vein is not directly associated with the blood flow near the root of the right lung. It is formed by the confluence of the right subclavian and right internal jugular veins, draining blood from the upper limb and head.
choiceRationales.B: The right subclavian vein is also not in direct proximity to the root of the right lung. It receives blood from the right upper limb and right side of the thorax.
choiceRationales.C: The accessory hemiazygos vein drains the left ninth to eleventh intercostal veins and may drain into the hemiazygos vein or directly into the azygos vein. It is not directly associated with the blood flow near the root of the right lung.
choiceRationales.D:

review.stem: A 52 year old female with a history of brain tumor and associated severe oropharyngeal dysphagia develops right lower lobe pneumonia after an episode of vomiting? Which of the following is the best reason that this type of aspiration pneumonia most commonly affects the right lower lung lobe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The right main bronchus is narrower than the left main bronchus

choices.label: B
choices.text: The right main bronchus is longer than the left main bronchus

choices.label: C
choices.text: The right lower lung lobe has poorer venous drainage than the other lobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The right main bronchus is straighter than the left main bronchus

review.explanation: The right lung is larger and heavier than the left, but is shorter and wider (so, A and B is wrong) because of the higher right dome of the diaphragm and the heart’s inclination to the left. The right main bronchus courses more vertically than the left (D is correct).

choiceRationales.A: This statement is not accurate. The right main bronchus is wider and more vertical than the left main bronchus. Therefore, aspiration is less likely to affect the right lower lobe due to a narrower bronchus.
choiceRationales.B: This statement is not accurate. The right main bronchus is shorter and wider than the left main bronchus. The length of the bronchus is not a significant factor in the predisposition to aspiration pneumonia.
choiceRationales.C: The venous drainage of the lung is not a primary factor in the predisposition to aspiration pneumonia. The main factors involve the anatomy of the bronchi and their relationship to the trachea.
choiceRationales.D: The right lung is larger and heavier than the left, but is shorter and wider (so, A and B is wrong) because of the higher right dome of the diaphragm and the heart’s inclination to the left. The right main bronchus courses more vertically than the left (D is correct).

review.stem: A neonatal baby was born with diabetes mellitus due to inadequate production of insulin. Cells in the endocrine portion of the pancreas that secrete insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin are derived from which of the following?
review.explanation: Isolated clumps of endodermal cells accumulate within the mesoderm to form islet cells. The islet cells form: alpha cells (A cells) that secrete the hormone glucagon, beta cells (B cells) that produce insulin and are the most abundant of the islet cells, delta cells (D cells) that secrete the hormone somatostatin, which is also produced by a number of other endocrine cells in the body.

choiceRationales.A: Mesoderm gives rise to various structures, including muscles, bones, and the cardiovascular system. However, the endocrine cells of the pancreas, such as those producing insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin, are derived from the endoderm.
choiceRationales.B: The proctoderm, also known as the anal ectoderm, contributes to the formation of the anus and portions of the anal canal. It is not involved in the development of the pancreas or its endocrine cells.
choiceRationales.C: Ectoderm contributes to the formation of the nervous system, skin, and other structures. It does not play a significant role in the development of the endocrine cells in the pancreas.
choiceRationales.D: Isolated clumps of endodermal cells accumulate within the mesoderm to form islet cells. The islet cells form: alpha cells (A cells) that secrete the hormone glucagon, beta cells (B cells) that produce insulin and are the most abundant of the islet cells, delta cells (D cells) that secrete the hormone somatostatin, which is also produced by a number of other endocrine cells in the body.

review.stem: Observation of a histologic preparation of muscle reveals striations and peripherally located nuclei. The use of histochemistry shows a strong staining reaction to succinic dehydrogenase. The same tissue prepared for electron microscopy shows many mitochondria in rows between the myofibrils and beneath the sarcolemma. Which one of the following is the best description of this tissue?
review.explanation: Skeletal muscle cells include red (slow contraction but does not fatigue easily) and white (fast contraction but fatigues easily), and intermediate. The redness of red muscle fibers was found to be due to myoglobin, and myoglobin was found to be correlated with aerobic metabolism due to abundant mitochondrial activity. (Succinic dehydrogenase is most sensitive to use to histologically detecting mitochondrial proliferation) The pale or white fibers with low aerobic potential were found to be well endowed with glycolytic enzymes that enabled them to obtain energy rapidly by the incomplete oxidation of glycogen (hence, fast fibers).

choiceRationales.A: This choice is incorrect. White muscle fibers are characterized by fewer mitochondria, pale appearance, and reliance on anaerobic metabolism. They typically have a centrally located nucleus and are adapted for rapid, forceful contractions. However, the described tissue exhibits peripherally located nuclei, strong staining for succinic dehydrogenase (a mitochondrial enzyme), and abundant mitochondria, which are not characteristic of white muscle fibers.
choiceRationales.B: This choice is incorrect. Cardiac muscle exhibits striations and centrally located nuclei, but it does not typically show a strong staining reaction to succinic dehydrogenase. Additionally, the arrangement of mitochondria between myofibrils and beneath the sarcolemma is more typical of skeletal muscle than cardiac muscle.
choiceRationales.C: Skeletal muscle cells include red (slow contraction but does not fatigue easily) and white (fast contraction but fatigues easily), and intermediate. The redness of red muscle fibers was found to be due to myoglobin, and myoglobin was found to be correlated with aerobic metabolism due to abundant mitochondrial activity. (Succinic dehydrogenase is most sensitive to use to histologically detecting mitochondrial proliferation) The pale or white fibers with low aerobic potential were found to be well endowed with glycolytic enzymes that enabled them to obtain energy rapidly by the incomplete oxidation of glycogen (hence, fast fibers).
choiceRationales.D: This choice is incorrect. Smooth muscle does not typically exhibit striations, and its appearance under electron microscopy differs from the description provided. Smooth muscle cells have a central nucleus and lack the well-defined sarcomere structure seen in striated muscles like skeletal and cardiac muscle.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 37 year old man is suffering from carcinoma of the skin of the penis. Cancer cells are likely to metastasize directly to which of the following lymph nodes?
review.explanation: The superficial inguinal nodes receive lymph from the penis, scrotum, buttocks, labia majora, and the lower parts of the vagina and anal canal. These nodes have efferent vessels that drain primarily into the external iliac and common iliac nodes and ultimately to the lumbar {aortic) nodes. The internal iliac nodes receive lymph from the up­ per part of the rectum, vagina, uterus, and other pelvic organs, and they drain into the common iliac nodes and then into the lumbar {aortic) nodes. Lymph vessels from the glans penis drain initially into the deep inguinal nodes and then into the external iliac nodes.

choiceRationales.A: The aortic (lumbar) nodes are not the primary drainage site for the skin of the penis. They typically receive lymphatic drainage from the pelvic and abdominal organs.
choiceRationales.B: The external iliac nodes are part of the lymphatic drainage pathway for the skin of the penis. Lymph from the superficial inguinal nodes, which receive drainage from the penis, scrotum, and other regions, drains into the external iliac nodes.
choiceRationales.C: The internal iliac nodes primarily receive lymph from the upper part of the rectum, vagina, uterus, and other pelvic organs. They are not the primary drainage site for the skin of the penis.
choiceRationales.D: The superficial inguinal nodes receive lymph from the penis, scrotum, buttocks, labia majora, and the lower parts of the vagina and anal canal. These nodes have efferent vessels that drain primarily into the external iliac and common iliac nodes and ultimately to the lumbar {aortic) nodes. The internal iliac nodes receive lymph from the up­ per part of the rectum, vagina, uterus, and other pelvic organs, and they drain into the common iliac nodes and then into the lumbar {aortic) nodes. Lymph vessels from the glans penis drain initially into the deep inguinal nodes and then into the external iliac nodes.

review.stem: 23 year old woman visits her obstetrician for an annual checkup. During vaginal examination, which of the following structures may be palpated?
review.explanation: The vagina extends between the vestibule and the cervix of the uterus, and the uterine cervix pierces the anterior wall of the vagina. During a vaginal examination, the uterine cervix can be palpated and assessed. The cervix is the lower part of the uterus that connects with the vagina.

choiceRationales.A: The clitoris is situated at the apex of the vestibule anteriorly. The body of the clitoris is composed of two corpora cavernosa covered by their ischiocavernosus muscles. Seen externally, and can be palpated, is the glans of the clitoris, partly hidden by the prepuce.
choiceRationales.B: The vagina extends between the vestibule and the cervix of the uterus, and the uterine cervix pierces the anterior wall of the vagina. During a vaginal examination, the uterine cervix can be palpated and assessed. The cervix is the lower part of the uterus that connects with the vagina.
choiceRationales.C: The fundus of the uterus is usually non-palpable in a non-gravid (non-pregnant) female. The fundus is the upper portion of the uterus, and it is located above the entrance of the fallopian tubes. It is typically not accessible through palpation during routine examinations.
choiceRationales.D: The urinary bladder apex is located at the anterior end and is not palpable. The fundus or base is located at the posteroinferior triangular position, and is most palpable when distended.

review.stem: A 60 year old man was observed in the clinic. As he walked, the affected limb is moved forward by the abduction and circumduction. Which of the following BEST describes the gait in this patient?
review.explanation:
Hemiplegic gait occurs because of poor control of the flexor muscles during swing phase and spasticity of the extensor muscles acting to lengthen the affected leg (compared with the healthy side). The ankle is abnormally flexed downward and inward (equinovarus deformity), and initial contact during stance is abnormal, along the lateral edge of the foot or forefoot. The knee is stiff, hyperextends during stance, and does not flex normally during swing. The contralateral step often advances just to meet the position of the paralyzed limb, instead of advancing normally beyond it.
Because the paralyzed leg is hyperextended, and therefore longer than the sound leg, the patient may drag the toe of the affected leg during swing or adopt abnormal movements to clear that limb during the swing phase. These movements include contralateral trunk lean, which raises the ipsilateral pelvis to clear the paralyzed leg, and circumduction, which describes the toe tracing a semicircle on the floor, first moving outward and then inward as it advances, instead of the normal straight forward movement.

choiceRationales.A: Parkinsonian gait is characterized by a shuffling walk with short steps, reduced arm swing, and difficulty initiating movements. Patients often exhibit festination, where they involuntarily start taking faster and faster steps, leading to a forward-leaning posture. Abduction and circumduction of limbs are not typically prominent features of Parkinsonian gait.
choiceRationales.B: Spastic gait is associated with muscle spasticity and stiffness, often seen in conditions affecting the upper motor neurons, such as in spastic cerebral palsy. The affected limb in spastic gait tends to be held stiffly, and circumduction or abduction movements are not characteristic.
choiceRationales.C:
Hemiplegic gait occurs because of poor control of the flexor muscles during swing phase and spasticity of the extensor muscles acting to lengthen the affected leg (compared with the healthy side). The ankle is abnormally flexed downward and inward (equinovarus deformity), and initial contact during stance is abnormal, along the lateral edge of the foot or forefoot. The knee is stiff, hyperextends during stance, and does not flex normally during swing. The contralateral step often advances just to meet the position of the paralyzed limb, instead of advancing normally beyond it.
Because the paralyzed leg is hyperextended, and therefore longer than the sound leg, the patient may drag the toe of the affected leg during swing or adopt abnormal movements to clear that limb during the swing phase. These movements include contralateral trunk lean, which raises the ipsilateral pelvis to clear the paralyzed leg, and circumduction, which describes the toe tracing a semicircle on the floor, first moving outward and then inward as it advances, instead of the normal straight forward movement.
choiceRationales.D: Steppage gait is associated with foot drop, a condition where the foot hangs with the toes pointing down, leading to an exaggerated lifting of the leg to avoid tripping. This gait pattern is often seen in conditions that affect the dorsiflexor muscles or the common fibular nerve. Abduction and circumduction movements are not typical features of steppage gait.

review.stem: A middle-aged coal miner injures his back after an accidental explosion. His MRI scan reveals that his spinal cord has shifted to the right because the lateral extensions of the pia mater were torn. Function of which of the following structures is MOST likely impaired?
review.explanation: This is the correct answer. The denticulate ligament is a series of delicate extensions of pia mater that attach to the arachnoid and help suspend the spinal cord within the vertebral canal. If the lateral extensions of the pia mater were torn, it could lead to a shift in the position of the spinal cord. The denticulate ligament is crucial for providing stability to the spinal cord.

choiceRationales.A: The coccygeal ligament is located at the base of the vertebral column and is not directly related to the spinal cord in the thoracic or cervical regions. Injuries to this ligament would not cause a shift in the spinal cord or impair its function.
choiceRationales.B: The tectorial membrane is a continuation of the posterior longitudinal ligament and is located in the cervical spine. It helps stabilize the spinal cord. However, it is not typically associated with lateral shifts of the spinal cord. Injuries to the tectorial membrane might affect stability but are less likely to cause a lateral shift.
choiceRationales.C: This is the correct answer. The denticulate ligament is a series of delicate extensions of pia mater that attach to the arachnoid and help suspend the spinal cord within the vertebral canal. If the lateral extensions of the pia mater were torn, it could lead to a shift in the position of the spinal cord. The denticulate ligament is crucial for providing stability to the spinal cord.
choiceRationales.D: The choroid plexus is primarily associated with the production of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the ventricles of the brain. It is not directly involved in spinal cord stability, and its impairment would not likely cause a shift in the spinal cord.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 65-year old presents with jaundice of 2 to 3 weeks duration, fatigue and increasing epigastric pain. The pain does not relate to eating. He has pale stools, dark urine, and elevated urinary and serum conjugated bilirubin. CT scan reveals a suspicious mass in the head of the pancreas adjacent to the descending duodenum. The gallbladder is significantly enlarged. Which of the following is the LIKELY cause of the elevated bilirubin?
review.explanation: This is the likely cause. A mass in the head of the pancreas adjacent to the descending duodenum could block the common bile duct, preventing the flow of bile into the duodenum. This obstruction would lead to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, resulting in jaundice, pale stools, and dark urine. The enlarged gallbladder is indicative of obstruction.

choiceRationales.A: A blocked cystic duct typically leads to the retention of bile in the gallbladder, causing symptoms like right upper quadrant pain, but it does not directly cause conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. This is less likely to be the cause of the elevated bilirubin in this patient.
choiceRationales.B: Viral hepatitis can cause elevated bilirubin levels, but the pattern of pale stools and dark urine, along with an enlarged gallbladder, is not typical for viral hepatitis. The imaging findings also suggest a pancreatic mass rather than hepatitis.
choiceRationales.C: Portal hypertension is associated with liver disease and can lead to elevated bilirubin. However, the clinical presentation, including epigastric pain, pale stools, and an enlarged gallbladder, is not consistent with portal hypertension. The focus on a mass in the pancreas points more toward a pancreatic etiology.
choiceRationales.D: This is the likely cause. A mass in the head of the pancreas adjacent to the descending duodenum could block the common bile duct, preventing the flow of bile into the duodenum. This obstruction would lead to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, resulting in jaundice, pale stools, and dark urine. The enlarged gallbladder is indicative of obstruction.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A bifid ureter or paired unilateral ureters result from partial or complete division of which of the following embryonic structures?
review.explanation: In bifid ureter, the ureters may join in the lower third of their course, may open through a common orifice into the bladder, or may open independently into the bladder. In the latter case, one ureter crosses its fellow and may produce urinary obstruction. The cause of bifid ureter is a premature division of the ureteric bud. Cases of double pelvis and double ureters may be found by chance on radiologic investigation of the urinary tract. They are more liable to become infected or to be the seat of calculus formation than a normal ureter.

choiceRationales.A: The metanephric mesoderm is involved in the formation of the metanephric kidney during embryonic development. However, the bifid ureter or paired unilateral ureters are primarily associated with the ureteric bud, not the metanephric mesoderm.
choiceRationales.B: In bifid ureter, the ureters may join in the lower third of their course, may open through a common orifice into the bladder, or may open independently into the bladder. In the latter case, one ureter crosses its fellow and may produce urinary obstruction. The cause of bifid ureter is a premature division of the ureteric bud. Cases of double pelvis and double ureters may be found by chance on radiologic investigation of the urinary tract. They are more liable to become infected or to be the seat of calculus formation than a normal ureter.
choiceRationales.C: The mesonephric duct gives rise to the male reproductive system, and its involvement is not directly related to the formation of the ureters.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 7 year old girl has difficulty breathing through her nose and is brought to her pediatrician. On examination, she is diagnosed with adenoids. Which of the following tonsils is enlarged?
review.explanation: Excessive hypertrophy of the lymphoid tissue, usually associated with infection, causes the pharyngeal tonsils to become enlarged; they are then commonly referred to as adenoids. Marked hypertrophy blocks the posterior nasal openings and causes the patient to snore loudly at night and to breathe through the open mouth. The close relationship of the infected lymphoid tissue to the auditory tube may be the cause of deafness and recurrent otitis media. Adenoidectomy is the treatment of choice for hypertrophied adenoids with infection. The nasal part of the pharynx may be viewed clinically by a mirror passed through the mouth.

choiceRationales.A: The lingual tonsil is located on the posterior part of the tongue, and its enlargement is not typically associated with difficulty breathing through the nose. Enlargement of the lingual tonsil may contribute to throat discomfort or difficulty swallowing.
choiceRationales.B: Excessive hypertrophy of the lymphoid tissue, usually associated with infection, causes the pharyngeal tonsils to become enlarged; they are then commonly referred to as adenoids. Marked hypertrophy blocks the posterior nasal openings and causes the patient to snore loudly at night and to breathe through the open mouth. The close relationship of the infected lymphoid tissue to the auditory tube may be the cause of deafness and recurrent otitis media. Adenoidectomy is the treatment of choice for hypertrophied adenoids with infection. The nasal part of the pharynx may be viewed clinically by a mirror passed through the mouth.
choiceRationales.C: The tubal tonsil is located near the openings of the auditory tubes into the nasopharynx. Enlargement of the tubal tonsil is less likely to cause significant nasal obstruction.
choiceRationales.D: The palatine tonsils are located on the sides of the oral cavity, and their enlargement is more commonly associated with a sore throat or difficulty swallowing rather than nasal obstruction.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 46 year old college football coach undergoes a radical prostatectomy for a malignant tumor in his prostate. Following surgery, he is incapable of achieving an erection. Which of the following nerves MOST likely damaged during surgery?
review.explanation: The pelvic splanchnic nerve contains preganglionic parasympa­thetic fibers, whereas the sacral splanchnic nerve contains preganglionic sympathetic fibers. Parasympathetic fibers are responsible for erection, whereas sympathetic fibers are involved with ejaculation. The right and left hypogastric nerves contain primarily sympathetic fibers and visceral sensory fibers. The dorsal nerve of the penis and the perineal nerve provide sensory nerve fibers.

choiceRationales.A: The pudendal nerve is primarily responsible for providing somatic motor innervation to the perineum and external genitalia. It plays a crucial role in the voluntary control of muscles involved in urination and defecation but is not the primary nerve involved in erection.
choiceRationales.B: The pelvic splanchnic nerve contains preganglionic parasympa­thetic fibers, whereas the sacral splanchnic nerve contains preganglionic sympathetic fibers. Parasympathetic fibers are responsible for erection, whereas sympathetic fibers are involved with ejaculation. The right and left hypogastric nerves contain primarily sympathetic fibers and visceral sensory fibers. The dorsal nerve of the penis and the perineal nerve provide sensory nerve fibers.
choiceRationales.C: The sacral splanchnic nerve contains preganglionic sympathetic fibers. While sympathetic activity is involved in ejaculation, it is not the primary contributor to erection.
choiceRationales.D: The dorsal nerve of the penis provides sensory innervation to the penis but is not the primary nerve responsible for initiating or maintaining an erection.

review.stem: A 70-year old woman often consults for swallowing difficulties and subsequent choking while eating food. Which of the following pairs of muscles is MOST instrumental in preventing food from entering the larynx and trachea during swallowing?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Levator veli palatini and Tensor veli palatine muscles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor and thyrohyoid muscles

review.explanation: The oblique arytenoid and aryepiglottic muscles tilt the ar­ytenoid cartilages and approximate them, assisting in closing of the larynx and preventing food from entering the larynx and trachea during the process of swallowing. The cricopharyngeus fibers of the inferior pharyngeal constrictors act as a sphincter that prevents air from entering the esophagus. Other muscles are not involved in closing or opening the airway.

choiceRationales.A: The sternohyoid and sternothyroid muscles are infrahyoid muscles responsible for depressing the hyoid bone and larynx during swallowing. However, they are not directly involved in preventing food from entering the larynx and trachea.
choiceRationales.B: These muscles are more involved in the elevation of the soft palate, contributing to the closure of the nasopharynx during swallowing. While they play a role in preventing nasal regurgitation, they are not primarily responsible for protecting the larynx and trachea.
choiceRationales.C: The oblique arytenoid and aryepiglottic muscles tilt the ar­ytenoid cartilages and approximate them, assisting in closing of the larynx and preventing food from entering the larynx and trachea during the process of swallowing. The cricopharyngeus fibers of the inferior pharyngeal constrictors act as a sphincter that prevents air from entering the esophagus. Other muscles are not involved in closing or opening the airway.
choiceRationales.D: These muscles are involved in the closure of the larynx during swallowing. The inferior pharyngeal constrictor, along with other pharyngeal muscles, contracts during swallowing, helping to propel the bolus downward. The thyrohyoid muscle assists in the upward movement of the larynx, contributing to the closure of the laryngeal inlet and preventing aspiration.

review.stem: A 55-year old complains of fecal incontinence. The most likely contributing factor to such a problem is atrophy, paralysis, or dysfunction of which of the following structures?
review.explanation:
The levator ani muscle consists of the puborectalis, pubococcygeus, and iliococcygeus. It supports and raises the pelvic floor. The coccygeus also supports and raises the pelvic floor.
Defecation is initiated by distention of the rectum which has filled from the sigmoid colon, and afferent impulses transmitted to the spinal cord by the pelvic splanchnic nerve.
Pubococcygeus and iliococcygeus contribute to lateral pressure to narrow the levator hiatus, and puborectalis muscle has a role in maintaining continence. Impaired levator ani contraction is strongly correlated with severity of fecal incontinence.
Fecal continence relies on two systems: A resistive and a capacitive system. The rectum that is a reservoir for stool represents the capacitive system. The resistive system is made up of the anal sphincters and the pubococcygeus muscle that closes the anal canal and maintains optimal intra abdominal pressure

choiceRationales.A: The coccygeus muscle is part of the levator ani muscle group. While it provides support to the pelvic organs, its primary function is not directly related to fecal continence. Dysfunction in this muscle alone is less likely to cause fecal incontinence.
choiceRationales.B: The iliococcygeus muscle is also part of the levator ani muscle group. It supports the pelvic organs and assists in maintaining fecal continence. Dysfunction in this muscle can contribute to fecal incontinence.
choiceRationales.C: The urogenital diaphragm is primarily involved in supporting the urogenital structures and maintaining urinary continence. It is less directly related to fecal continence.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A radiograph of a 34-year-old woman reveals a perforation of the stomach in which the gastric contents have spilled into the lesser sac. The general surgeon has opened the gastrosplenic artery. Which of the following vessels is most likely involved?
review.explanation: The left gastroepiploic artery runs through the lienogastric ligament, and hence, it is the artery most likely injured. The splenic artery is found in the lienorenal ligament The right and left gastric arteries run within the lesser omentum. The gastroduodenal artery descends between the duodenum and the head of the pancreas.

choiceRationales.A: The left gastric artery typically arises from the celiac trunk and runs along the lesser curvature of the stomach. It supplies the upper part of the stomach and often anastomoses with the right gastric artery. However, in the scenario described, the left gastric artery is less likely to be involved in the perforation and spillage into the lesser sac.
choiceRationales.B: The gastroduodenal artery is a branch of the common hepatic artery and supplies the anterosuperior part of the duodenum. It does not typically supply the stomach directly. Therefore, it is less likely to be involved in the gastric perforation described.
choiceRationales.C: The left gastroepiploic artery runs through the lienogastric ligament, and hence, it is the artery most likely injured. The splenic artery is found in the lienorenal ligament The right and left gastric arteries run within the lesser omentum. The gastroduodenal artery descends between the duodenum and the head of the pancreas.
choiceRationales.D: The right gastric artery is a branch of the common hepatic artery and supplies the lesser curvature of the stomach. In the scenario described, where the perforation involves the lesser sac, the right gastric artery is less likely to be directly involved.

review.stem: A 17-year-old boy with a stab wound received multiple injuries on the upper part of the arm and required surgery. If the brachial artery were ligated at its origin, which of the following arteries would supply blood to the profunda brachii artery?
review.explanation: The posterior humeral circumflex artery anastomoses with an ascending branch of the profunda brachii artery, whereas the lateral tho­racic and subscapular arteries do not. The superior ulnar collateral and radial recurrent arteries arise inferior to the origin of the profunda brachii artery.

choiceRationales.A: The superior ulnar collateral artery arises from the brachial artery and contributes to the blood supply of the elbow joint. However, its course is mainly inferior to the origin of the profunda brachii artery. Therefore, it does not serve as a direct source of blood for the profunda brachii artery.
choiceRationales.B: The subscapular artery is a major branch of the axillary artery. While it contributes to the blood supply of the shoulder region, it does not directly supply the profunda brachii artery.
choiceRationales.C: The posterior humeral circumflex artery anastomoses with an ascending branch of the profunda brachii artery, whereas the lateral tho­racic and subscapular arteries do not. The superior ulnar collateral and radial recurrent arteries arise inferior to the origin of the profunda brachii artery.
choiceRationales.D: The lateral thoracic artery is a branch of the axillary artery that primarily supplies the lateral chest wall and breast tissue. It is not directly involved in supplying the profunda brachii artery.

review.stem: During a domestic dispute, a 17-year-old boy receives a deep stab wound around the superior angle of the scapula near the medial border, which injures both the dorsal scapular and spinal accessory nerves. Such an injury could result in paralysis or weakness of which of the following muscles?
review.explanation:
The trapezius is solely innervated by the spinal accessory nerve, or cranial nerve XI, which crosses the posterior cervical triangle superficially before diving vertically along the deep surface of the trapezius.
Both rhomboid muscles are innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve, with its fibers predominantly derived from the C5 nerve root with minor contributions from C4 or C6.
Paralysis to the trapezius muscle, like serratus anterior paralysis, is primarily neurogenic, but from injuries to the spinal accessory nerve. Similarly, rhomboid paralysis tends to be primarily neurogenic in nature, involving the dorsal scapular nerve.

choiceRationales.A:
The dorsal scapular nerve innervates the rhomboid minor and rhomboid major muscles. Injury to this nerve could result in weakness or paralysis of these muscles.
The latissimus dorsi is primarily innervated by the thoracodorsal nerve, which is a branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus and not typically affected by injuries to the dorsal scapular nerve.
choiceRationales.B:
The spinal accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI) innervates the trapezius muscle. Injury to this nerve could lead to weakness or paralysis of the trapezius muscle.
Serratus posterior superior is not typically innervated by the dorsal scapular or spinal accessory nerves.
choiceRationales.C:
The trapezius is solely innervated by the spinal accessory nerve, or cranial nerve XI, which crosses the posterior cervical triangle superficially before diving vertically along the deep surface of the trapezius.
Both rhomboid muscles are innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve, with its fibers predominantly derived from the C5 nerve root with minor contributions from C4 or C6.
Paralysis to the trapezius muscle, like serratus anterior paralysis, is primarily neurogenic, but from injuries to the spinal accessory nerve. Similarly, rhomboid paralysis tends to be primarily neurogenic in nature, involving the dorsal scapular nerve.
choiceRationales.D:
The splenius cervicis is primarily innervated by the posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves.
The sternocleidomastoid is innervated by the accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI) and not typically affected by injuries to the dorsal scapular nerve.

review.explanation: The greater splanchnic nerves contain visceral afferent (VA) and preganglionic sympathetic visceral efferent (VE) fibers.

choiceRationales.A: The sacral splanchnic nerves carry preganglionic sympathetic fibers that synapse in the inferior mesenteric ganglion. Postganglionic sympathetic fibers then continue to their target structures, including blood vessels, smooth muscle, and glands in the pelvic region.
choiceRationales.B: The sacral splanchnic nerves are part of the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system, and they carry preganglionic sympathetic fibers, not parasympathetic fibers. Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers to the pelvic viscera typically originate from the sacral segments of the spinal cord (pelvic splanchnic nerves).
choiceRationales.C: The greater splanchnic nerves contain visceral afferent (VA) and preganglionic sympathetic visceral efferent (VE) fibers.
choiceRationales.D: Postganglionic parasympathetic fibers are typically carried by the vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) in the pelvic region, not the sacral splanchnic nerves.

review.explanation: This is a classic location for auscultating the mitral valve. The fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line is commonly referred to as the "apex" of the heart, and it is where the mitral valve sounds are best heard.

choiceRationales.A: This location is not commonly used for auscultating the mitral valve. The second left intercostal space is typically associated with pulmonic valve auscultation.

review.stem: A patient is rushed to the operating room for an emergent cholecystectomy because of cholecystitis. While locating landmarks before surgical resection of an infected gallbladder, the surgeon recalls a porto-caval anastomosis. Which of the following pairs of veins form a porto-caval anastomosis?
review.explanation: Portal-caval anastomoses occur between the left gastric vein and esophageal vein of the azygos, the superior rectal and middle or inferior rectal veins, paraumbilical and superficial epigastric veins, and retrocolic veins and twigs of the renal vein. The hepatic veins and the IVC are systemic or caval veins. The left and right gastric veins belong to the portal venous system. The inferior and superficial epigastric veins and the suprarenal and renal veins are systemic veins.

choiceRationales.A: The left gastric vein and right gastric vein are veins that drain the lesser curvature of the stomach. They form an anastomosis with esophageal veins, creating a connection between the portal system and the systemic circulation. However, it's more related to esophageal varices than a direct porto-caval anastomosis.
choiceRationales.B: he inferior epigastric vein and superficial epigastric vein are tributaries of the external iliac vein. They do not directly participate in porto-caval anastomosis.
choiceRationales.C: Portal-caval anastomoses occur between the left gastric vein and esophageal vein of the azygos, the superior rectal and middle or inferior rectal veins, paraumbilical and superficial epigastric veins, and retrocolic veins and twigs of the renal vein. The hepatic veins and the IVC are systemic or caval veins. The left and right gastric veins belong to the portal venous system. The inferior and superficial epigastric veins and the suprarenal and renal veins are systemic veins.
choiceRationales.D: The suprarenal vein and renal vein are veins associated with the adrenal gland and kidney, respectively. They do not participate in porto-caval anastomosis.

review.stem: A possible malignant mass from the liver of a neonate with cerebral palsy was resected. The pediatric surgeon divides the round ligament of the liver during surgery. A fibrous remnant of which of the following fetal vessels is severed?
review.explanation: The left umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. It usually closes after birth and forms the ligamentum teres (round ligament of the liver). This is the structure divided during the surgery.

choiceRationales.A: The ductus arteriosus is a fetal blood vessel connecting the pulmonary artery to the aorta. It usually closes shortly after birth but is not related to the round ligament of the liver.
choiceRationales.B: The ductus venosus is a fetal blood vessel that shunts oxygenated blood from the umbilical vein directly to the inferior vena cava, bypassing the liver. After birth, it usually closes and forms the ligamentum venosum, which is a fibrous remnant. However, the ductus venosus is not directly related to the round ligament of the liver.
choiceRationales.C: The left umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. It usually closes after birth and forms the ligamentum teres (round ligament of the liver). This is the structure divided during the surgery.
choiceRationales.D: The right umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. It usually closes after birth and becomes the ligamentum venosum, but this is not directly associated with the round ligament of the liver.

review.stem: A 64-year-old man presents with back pain, weakness, and shortness of breath. On examination, he has an aneurysm of the abdominal aorta at the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm. Which of the following pairs of structures would MOST likely be compressed?
review.explanation: The aortic hiatus of the diaphragm transmits the azygos vein and thoracic duct. The vagus nerve passes through the esophageal hiatus, and the right phrenic nerve may run through the vena caval hiatus.

choiceRationales.A: The aortic hiatus typically does not transmit the esophagus; instead, it is the esophageal hiatus. However, the vagus nerve passes through both the esophageal hiatus and the aortic hiatus. Compression could lead to symptoms related to vagal dysfunction and, to some extent, esophageal compression.
choiceRationales.B: The thoracic duct and vagus nerve do not share a common passage. The thoracic duct usually ascends alongside the vertebral column and may not be directly influenced by an abdominal aortic aneurysm.
choiceRationales.C: The aortic hiatus of the diaphragm transmits the azygos vein and thoracic duct. The vagus nerve passes through the esophageal hiatus, and the right phrenic nerve may run through the vena caval hiatus.
choiceRationales.D: Similar to option A, the vagus nerve passes through the aortic hiatus alongside the azygos vein. Compression could result in vagal dysfunction.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 47-year old man cannot move his eye laterally. Which of the following conditions would cause this inability to move eye?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Occlusion of the posterior cerebral artery

review.explanation: The abducens nerve, which innervates the lateral rectus muscle, runs through the middle of the cavernous sinus. The other conditions listed do not injure the abducens nerve. A tumor in the pituitary gland may injure the optic chiasma, causing bitemporal hemianopsia.

choiceRationales.A: A tumor of the pituitary gland is less likely to cause an inability to move the eye laterally. The cranial nerve responsible for lateral eye movement is the abducens nerve (CN VI), and its nucleus is located in the pontine tegmentum.
choiceRationales.B: The abducens nerve, which innervates the lateral rectus muscle, runs through the middle of the cavernous sinus. The other conditions listed do not injure the abducens nerve. A tumor in the pituitary gland may injure the optic chiasma, causing bitemporal hemianopsia.
choiceRationales.C: An occlusion of the posterior cerebral artery is more likely to affect the occipital lobe, leading to visual disturbances rather than causing an inability to move the eye laterally.
choiceRationales.D: Infection in the maxillary sinus is less likely to directly affect eye movements. The maxillary sinus is not in direct proximity to the structures involved in eye movement.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 60-year-old heavy smoker has an advanced lung cancer that spread into her right third intercostal space posterior to the midaxillary line. If cancer cells are carried in the venous drainage, they would travel first to which of the following veins?
review.explanation: The superior in­tercostal vein is formed by the union of the second, third, and fourth posterior intercostal veins and drains into the azygos vein on the right and the brachiocephalic vein on the left. The azygos vein drains into the SVC. The hemiazygos vein usually drains into the azygos vein.

choiceRationales.A: The hemiazygos vein usually drains into the azygos vein. While it is involved in the venous drainage of the posterior thoracic wall, it is not the primary route for cancer cells from the described lung location.
choiceRationales.B: The superior in­tercostal vein is formed by the union of the second, third, and fourth posterior intercostal veins and drains into the azygos vein on the right and the brachiocephalic vein on the left. The azygos vein drains into the SVC. The hemiazygos vein usually drains into the azygos vein.
choiceRationales.C: The azygos vein is a major vessel in the venous drainage of the posterior thoracic wall. It receives blood from the right superior intercostal vein and plays a crucial role in carrying cancer cells from the described lung location toward the SVC.
choiceRationales.D: The right brachiocephalic vein receives blood from the azygos vein, making it a crucial part of the route for venous drainage from the described lung location. The blood then continues through the superior vena cava.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem:
A 37-year-old patient has an infectious inflammation of the dural venous sinus closest to the
pituitary gland and a secondary thrombus formation. Which of the following is the MOST likely site of
infection?
review.explanation: The dural venous sinus nearest the pituitary gland is the cavernous sinus. Cavernous sinus thrombophlebitis is an infectious inflammation of the sinus that may produce meningitis, papilledema, exophthalmos, and ophthalmoplegia. The other sinuses listed are not closely associated with the pituitary gland.

choiceRationales.A: The straight sinus is located at the junction of the falx cerebri and the tentorium cerebelli. It is not in close proximity to the pituitary gland. Infections in the straight sinus are less likely to affect the pituitary gland directly.
choiceRationales.B: The sigmoid sinus is a continuation of the transverse sinus and is located in the posterior cranial fossa. It is not directly associated with the pituitary gland. Infections in the sigmoid sinus may cause issues, but they are not likely to impact the pituitary gland as much as the cavernous sinus.
choiceRationales.C: The superior petrosal sinus drains into the transverse sinus and is not in close proximity to the pituitary gland. Infections in this sinus are less likely to affect the pituitary gland.
choiceRationales.D: The dural venous sinus nearest the pituitary gland is the cavernous sinus. Cavernous sinus thrombophlebitis is an infectious inflammation of the sinus that may produce meningitis, papilledema, exophthalmos, and ophthalmoplegia. The other sinuses listed are not closely associated with the pituitary gland.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem:
A 28-year-old man presents to the ER after a high-speed motor vehicle accident. Neurologic exam
showed the lowest functioning neurologic level is C5. Which is the LIKELY finding in this patient given
the neurologic assessment level?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flexion of the distal interphalangeal joints is intact; finger adduction and abduction is not functional

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sensation is intact over and just inferior to the clavicle; sensation is not intact over the lateral aspect of the shoulder and deltoid region

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deltoid and biceps motor function is intact; extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis muscles are not functional

choices.label: D
choices.text: The anal sphincter is flaccid when the glans penis is squeezed

review.explanation: This description is consistent with a C5 neurological level. With this injury level, sensation is preserved just inferior to the clavicle, and there is loss of sensation over the lateral aspect of the shoulder and the deltoid region.

choiceRationales.A: This finding is characteristic of a C8 spinal cord injury level. In this case, with a C5 neurological level, it is less likely, as the symptoms would typically manifest at a higher neurological level.
choiceRationales.B: This description is consistent with a C5 neurological level. With this injury level, sensation is preserved just inferior to the clavicle, and there is loss of sensation over the lateral aspect of the shoulder and the deltoid region.
choiceRationales.C: This finding is not consistent with a C5 neurological level. In C5 injuries, there would typically be impairment of deltoid and biceps function.
choiceRationales.D: This is indicative of a lower motor neuron lesion and suggests injury at the sacral segments. It is not directly related to the C5 neurological level described in this case.

A 35-year-old woman is admitted to the ER with severe left abdominal and back pain. Radiographic evaluation reveals that the left ureter is blocked with a kidney stone. Because the ureter is completely obstructed, an emergency surgical procedure must be performed. The MOST reliable landmark for the
identification of the ureter is that the left ureter is anterior to the left.
review.explanation: The left ureter crosses anterior to the common iliac vessels at the pelvic brim. This relationship can be used as a reliable landmark for identifying the ureter during surgery.

choiceRationales.A: The left renal vein courses anterior to the abdominal aorta, and it typically passes anterior to the left renal artery. While it is in proximity to the left ureter, it is not a reliable landmark for identifying the ureter in cases of obstruction.
choiceRationales.B: The left ureter crosses anterior to the common iliac vessels at the pelvic brim. This relationship can be used as a reliable landmark for identifying the ureter during surgery.
choiceRationales.C: The gonadal arteries (testicular or ovarian) originate from the abdominal aorta and run inferiorly. The left ureter is generally anterior to the left gonadal artery.
choiceRationales.D: The inferior epigastric artery arises from the external iliac artery and runs superiorly. It is not directly related to the left ureter in terms of its anatomical position.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 56-year old woman was diagnosed with bitemporal hemianopia. Where is the lesion of this visual field defect?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lesion of the tip of an occipital lobe

review.explanation: Bitemporal hemianopia is characteristic of a lesion at the optic chiasm. The optic chiasm is where the optic nerves from both eyes partially decussate (cross). A lesion here can result in loss of peripheral vision on both sides (temporal fields) while sparing the central vision.

choiceRationales.A: The calcarine cortex is located in the occipital lobe, specifically in the primary visual cortex (V1). A lesion in this area would likely result in contralateral homonymous hemianopia, not bitemporal hemianopia.
choiceRationales.B: Similar to the explanation for choice (a), a lesion in the occipital lobe would typically result in homonymous hemianopia, not bitemporal hemianopia.
choiceRationales.C: Bitemporal hemianopia is characteristic of a lesion at the optic chiasm. The optic chiasm is where the optic nerves from both eyes partially decussate (cross). A lesion here can result in loss of peripheral vision on both sides (temporal fields) while sparing the central vision.
choiceRationales.D: A lesion behind the optic chiasm would affect the optic tracts or other visual pathway structures. However, such a lesion would not typically result in bitemporal hemianopia; instead, it could cause homonymous hemianopia on one side.

review.stem:
A 38-year-old man infected with HIV for the past 10 years is admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain for 3 days duration. PE shows abdominal distention and absent bowel sounds. An abdominal CT scan shows a mass lesion involving the ileum. He undergoes surgery to remove an area of bowel obstruction in the ileum. Gross examination of the specimen shows a form, white mass, 10 cm long and 3 cm at its greatest depth. The mass has infiltrated through the wall of the ileum. Histologic studies show a mitotically active population of
CD19+ lymphoid cells with prominent nuclei and nucleoli. Molecular analysis is MOST likely to show which of the following viral genomes in the lymphoid cells?
review.explanation: EBV is strongly associated with various lymphoproliferative disorders in individuals with HIV, including primary central nervous system lymphoma and systemic B-cell lymphomas. The description of a mass lesion in the ileum with mitotically active CD19+ lymphoid cells is suggestive of a B-cell lymphoma. The most common subtype associated with HIV is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Molecular analysis is likely to show the presence of Epstein-Barr virus DNA in the lymphoid cells.

choiceRationales.A: Cytomegalovirus is associated with opportunistic infections in individuals with HIV, but it does not typically present as a mass lesion in the ileum. CMV infection in the gastrointestinal tract can cause ulcers, colitis, or enteritis, but the described form, white mass infiltrating through the wall of the ileum, is not typical for CMV.
choiceRationales.B: HTLV-1 is associated with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. However, the histologic description and presentation of the mass lesion in the ileum do not match the typical features of HTLV-1-associated lymphoma.
choiceRationales.C: Human herpesvirus 8 (also called Kaposi sarcoma herpesvirus) is found in the spindle cells of Kaposi sarcoma and in body cavity B-cell lymphomas in patients with AIDS.
choiceRationales.D: EBV is strongly associated with various lymphoproliferative disorders in individuals with HIV, including primary central nervous system lymphoma and systemic B-cell lymphomas. The description of a mass lesion in the ileum with mitotically active CD19+ lymphoid cells is suggestive of a B-cell lymphoma. The most common subtype associated with HIV is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Molecular analysis is likely to show the presence of Epstein-Barr virus DNA in the lymphoid cells.

review.stem: A 58-year-old man is admitted due to left flank pain. Blood exam indicates hematuria and anemia. MRI reveals that blood flow in the left renal vein is being occluded by an arterial aneurysm where the vein crosses the aorta. The aneurysm is MOST likely located in which artery?
review.explanation: The left renal vein courses between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Therefore, an aneurysm causing compression or occlusion of the left renal vein is MOST likely located in the superior mesenteric artery.

choiceRationales.A: The left colic artery is not directly related to the left renal vein's course between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery.
choiceRationales.B: The left renal vein courses between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Therefore, an aneurysm causing compression or occlusion of the left renal vein is MOST likely located in the superior mesenteric artery.
choiceRationales.C: The inferior mesenteric artery is not typically associated with the course of the left renal vein.
choiceRationales.D: The celiac artery, or celiac trunk, is not directly involved in the course of the left renal vein between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed with prostate cancer following a digital rectal examination. For the resection of prostate cancer, it is important to know that the prostatic ducts open into or on which of the following structures?
review.explanation: Ducts from the prostate gland open into the prostatic sinus, which is a groove on either side of the urethral crest. The prostate gland receives the ejaculatory duct, which opens into the prostatic urethra on the seminal colliculus (a prominent elevation of the urethral crest) just lateral to the prostatic utricle, which is a small blind pouch. The bulbourethral gland lies on the lateral side of the membranous urethra within the deep perineal space, but its duct opens into the bulbous portion of the spongy (penile) urethra.

choiceRationales.A: The prostatic utricle is a small, blind-ended pouch located in the midline of the prostatic urethra. It is a remnant of the Müllerian ducts and is not the structure where prostatic ducts open. The prostatic utricle is typically lateral to the ejaculatory duct openings.
choiceRationales.B: Ducts from the prostate gland open into the prostatic sinus, which is a groove on either side of the urethral crest. The prostate gland receives the ejaculatory duct, which opens into the prostatic urethra on the seminal colliculus (a prominent elevation of the urethral crest) just lateral to the prostatic utricle, which is a small blind pouch. The bulbourethral gland lies on the lateral side of the membranous urethra within the deep perineal space, but its duct opens into the bulbous portion of the spongy (penile) urethra.
choiceRationales.C: The seminal colliculus, also known as the verumontanum, is a ridge in the posterior urethra where the ejaculatory ducts and prostatic ducts open. It is a key anatomical landmark during surgery for prostate cancer.
choiceRationales.D: The spongy urethra is the portion of the male urethra that runs through the penis. Prostatic ducts do not open directly into the spongy urethra; instead, they release their secretions into the prostatic urethra, which is located above the spongy urethra.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A patient bleeding from the shoulder secondary to a knife wound is in fair condition because there is vascular anastomosis around the shoulder. Which of the following arteries is most likely a direct branch of the subclavian artery that is involved in the anastomosis?
review.explanation: The dorsal scapular artery arises directly from the third part of the subclavian artery and replaces the deep (descending) branch of the transverse cervical artery. The suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries are branches of the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian artery. The thoracoacromial artery is a short trunk from the first or second part of the axillary artery and has pectoral, clavicular, acromial, and deltoid branches.

choiceRationales.A: The circumflex scapular artery is typically a branch of the subscapular artery, which itself arises from the axillary artery. It is not a direct branch of the subclavian artery.
choiceRationales.B: The dorsal scapular artery arises directly from the third part of the subclavian artery and replaces the deep (descending) branch of the transverse cervical artery. The suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries are branches of the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian artery. The thoracoacromial artery is a short trunk from the first or second part of the axillary artery and has pectoral, clavicular, acromial, and deltoid branches.
choiceRationales.C: The suprascapular artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk, which typically arises from the first part of the subclavian artery. While it is not a direct branch of the subclavian artery, it contributes to the blood supply around the shoulder and scapula.
choiceRationales.D: The thoracoacromial artery arises from the second part of the axillary artery, not directly from the subclavian artery. It branches into pectoral, deltoid, acromial, and clavicular branches and is not a direct branch of the subclavian artery.

review.subject: anatomy
review.stem: A 22-year old man has a gonorrheal infection that has infiltrated the space between the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm and the superficial perineal fascia. Which of the following structures might be inflamed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Membranous part of the male urethra

review.explanation: The bulb of the penis is located in the superficial perineal space between the perineal membrane of the urogenital diaphragm and the membranous layer of the superficial perineal fascia (Colles fascia). All of the other structures are found in the deep perineal space (pouch).

choiceRationales.A: The membranous part of the male urethra is located within the urogenital diaphragm, but it lies deeper within the structure than the space described in the scenario. Inflammation of this part typically results in urethritis, which is common in gonorrheal infections, but it wouldn't be the structure directly affected by inflammation in the space described.
choiceRationales.B: The bulbourethral glands, also known as Cowper's glands, are located within the deep perineal space. They are responsible for secreting a clear, viscous fluid into the urethra during sexual arousal. Inflammation of these glands can occur due to infection, but they are not in the space mentioned in the scenario.
choiceRationales.C: The bulb of the penis is located in the superficial perineal space between the perineal membrane of the urogenital diaphragm and the membranous layer of the superficial perineal fascia (Colles fascia). All of the other structures are found in the deep perineal space (pouch).
choiceRationales.D: The deep transverse perineal muscle is located within the deep perineal space. It runs transversely across the perineum and plays a role in supporting the pelvic viscera. Inflammation of this muscle is less common but can occur in conditions such as perineal trauma or infection.

A 63-year old man presents with splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, persistent fever, night sweats, and
weight loss. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy are scheduled. The BEST place to take a sample bone marrow is in the ?
review.explanation: The iliac crest is a commonly used and preferred site for bone marrow aspiration. The posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) is often the chosen point for this procedure. It provides easy access to the bone marrow with a lower risk of complications.

choiceRationales.A: While the sternum contains red marrow and can be used for bone marrow aspirations, it is not the preferred site due to the risk of injury to the underlying structures, including the heart and major vessels.
choiceRationales.B: Similar to the sternum, the scapula is not a typical site for bone marrow aspiration. It is not a weight-bearing bone and does not contain as much red marrow as the sites commonly chosen for aspirations.
choiceRationales.C: The iliac crest is a commonly used and preferred site for bone marrow aspiration. The posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) is often the chosen point for this procedure. It provides easy access to the bone marrow with a lower risk of complications.
choiceRationales.D: The humerus is not a typical site for bone marrow aspiration. The iliac crest is generally preferred over other bones for this procedure.

review.stem:
A 47-year old woman is admitted due to sharp and constant abdominal pain, beginning in the epigastric region and radiated bilaterally around the chest to just below the scapulae. The pain later became localized in the right hypochondrium. Similar but milder attacks were noted after hearty meals, is moderately overweight.
PE showed marked tenderness in the right hypochondriac region and some rigidity of the abdominal musculature. An x-ray without contrast medium shows numerous calcified stones in the region of the gallbladder. There was no sign of jaundice. Diffuse pain referred to the epigastric region and radiating
circumferentially around the chest is the result of afferent fibers that travel via which of the following nerves?
review.explanation:
Visceral afferent pain fibers from the gallbladder travel through the celiac plexus, hence along the greater splanchnic nerves to levels T5 to T9 of the spinal cord. Thus, pain originating from the gallbladder will be referred to the dermatomes served by T5 to T9, which include a band from the infrascapular region to the epigastrium.
Parietal pain would be localized to the right hypochondriac region (below the ribs where the gallbladder is located) by intercostals and can also be referred to the right shoulder via the phrenic nerve.

choiceRationales.A: Intercostal nerves run between the ribs and are primarily responsible for innervating the intercostal muscles and skin of the chest. They are not typically involved in the referred pain from the gallbladder.
choiceRationales.B: he vagus nerve carries parasympathetic fibers and is involved in the innervation of abdominal organs. However, referred pain from the gallbladder, particularly to the right shoulder or scapula, is not primarily mediated by the vagus nerve.
choiceRationales.C: The phrenic nerve innervates the diaphragm and is not a major contributor to the referred pain from the gallbladder. Referred pain from the gallbladder tends to involve the shoulder or scapular region, not the diaphragmatic area.
choiceRationales.D:
Visceral afferent pain fibers from the gallbladder travel through the celiac plexus, hence along the greater splanchnic nerves to levels T5 to T9 of the spinal cord. Thus, pain originating from the gallbladder will be referred to the dermatomes served by T5 to T9, which include a band from the infrascapular region to the epigastrium.
Parietal pain would be localized to the right hypochondriac region (below the ribs where the gallbladder is located) by intercostals and can also be referred to the right shoulder via the phrenic nerve.
